summary: Fifth working cycle of the continuous-openui-local-2 lineage (driver cycle_index=6; an initialized-only cycle-5 attempt against pre-fix code crashed before campaign completion -- see harness_signals below -- and does not count as this lineage's cycle 5 per contracts.md's 'initialized-only/crashed campaign does not replace the latest completed handoff' rule). This session's job was the queued retry_measurement for c4's champion-confirmation cycle (held_out wall-timeout, frozen_manifest_sha256=d136c228a5a967e6884abdbfd2d5de46f6700bd1a110ccdd88fc772a07d30a1f). The first invocation of the supervised driver against the unmodified repo crashed immediately with RuntimeError('unsupported automatic frozen replay arm: confirm') before running any train/eval subprocess: the champion-queue '-confirm'/'-promote' arms (Change C/D) are not `_SCREENING_ARM_BANK` slugs, and the frozen-replay successor matrix was built through the generic thrash-rotation branch, which never contained a '-confirm' experiment id for `_apply_frozen_replay` to patch onto -- this is the first cycle in this lineage to attempt a frozen replay of a confirmation cycle, so the gap was previously unexercised. Fixed with `_frozen_replay_champion_levers` (scripts/run_autotrain_continuous.py, commit 90021cad314162099f2b3d80389e1b7c0287ba04): recovers the frozen candidate's champion-queue slug and rebuilds confirm_levers/promote_levers from the frozen candidate's own lever knobs so the successor matrix is built through the same branch that produced the original arm; `_apply_frozen_replay` now also accepts 'confirm'/'promote' as known replay slugs. 4 new regression tests added; full tests/test_scripts/test_run_autotrain_continuous.py suite (106 passed, 1 skipped) and verify_version_stamps --check both clean before commit. After the fix, the retry re-ran cleanly: it correctly reused c4's completed training checkpoints (no train_summary.json written this cycle; evaluate_model invoked with --checkpoint pointing at c4's runs) and only re-ran evaluate_model, exactly matching contracts.md's 'training completed but evaluation did not -> frozen replay resumes at evaluation instead of retraining' rule. Both arms' smoke suite (n=3) completed and scored bit-identical again (parse_rate=1.0/1.0, meaningful_program_rate=0.3333/0.3333, structural_similarity=0.4167/0.4167, binder_reference_f1=0.9524/0.9524; latency control p50=9779.53ms vs confirm p50=10369.86ms). held_out again did not finish on either arm: `decode_progress.json` shows both arms interrupted mid-suite with processed_record_n=3 of 5 (measurement_complete=false, ~7.2-7.4s/record mean this attempt), so the evaluate_model stage was killed by the harness wall-time guard a second time, structurally identical to c4's timeout. This confirms the harness crash and the wall-timeout are two independent, now-separated findings: the crash is fixed and verified resolved; the wall-timeout is reproduced honestly and is not a code defect -- it is decode-compute-bound (see eval_feasibility_confirmation below), the same class of problem as the parked continuous-openui-local lineage's test_data_scaleup_v1 finding, just triggered at a smaller record count (8 vs 12) because promotion's smoke+held_out combination is close to 2x over the fixed ~70s two-arm-split budget regardless of which record set is chosen (all four `_DEFAULT_EVAL_VERSION_CANDIDATES` snapshots carry the same held_out=5/smoke=3 suite sizes). No fix was attempted for the wall-timeout itself: MAX_RUN_MINUTES is a fixed architecture invariant, `_arm_wall_minutes`'s symmetric two-arm split is already at that ceiling for both screening and promotion roles (stage_wall_minutes_for_role returns the same MAX_RUN_MINUTES-clamped value for both), and the existing `_feasible_eval_version`/`_eval_version_fits_arm_budget` guard (added for the parked lineage's finding) already correctly identifies that no candidate eval snapshot fits promotion's suite requirement and by design falls back to an honest measurement_incomplete rather than blocking a fresh cycle -- there is no smaller held_out suite to substitute (all candidates carry held_out=5) and shrinking it would weaken the ship gate's held-out sample size, which is out of scope. Positive=false, stack_layer=false, stack_action=no_stack_layer_non_positive (the code fix is a harness-repair delta, tracked separately from model-positive classification -- see recommendation below on whether to push it).

eval_feasibility_confirmation.note: eval_version=e938_role_safe_all_targets_v2, eval_suites=smoke,held_out (8 records total: smoke=3, held_out=5). decode_progress.json for both arms shows measurement_complete=false, status=interrupted, processed_record_n=3/5 on held_out, mean total_ms per held_out record ~7.2-7.4s this attempt (~11s/record measured on c4's attempt -- consistent order of magnitude, some variance). All four snapshots in _DEFAULT_EVAL_VERSION_CANDIDATES (e938_role_safe_all_targets_v2, e842_harness_owned_slots_v1, e827_target_slots_only_v4, e763_symbol_only_eval_r2_20260722) carry identical smoke=3/held_out=5 suite sizes, so `_feasible_eval_version`'s candidate search cannot find one that fits promotion's suites within the ~70s arm budget minus overhead -- it correctly falls back to the default per its documented design rather than raising, which is why this is an honest measurement_incomplete rather than a hard failure. This is a decode-compute-bound structural limit given MAX_RUN_MINUTES=3, not a budget-sizing bug: stage_wall_minutes_for_role returns the policy-max (3, clamped to MAX_RUN_MINUTES) for both screening and promotion roles, and _arm_wall_minutes's symmetric two-arm split off MAX_HARNESS_WALL_SECONDS already dominates that value for both roles alike, so there is no slack to reallocate toward promotion's larger suite set without either violating MAX_RUN_MINUTES or reducing to fewer than the required 1-control/1-candidate arms.
